seo.title: Hollis & Son | Asheville Real Estate, a Mother and Son Team
seo.description: Ruth and Sam Hollis, a mother and son real estate team in Asheville, NC. Thirty years of selling mountain homes, honest advice on what to fix before you sell.

hero.headline: We're Ruth and Sam Hollis, a mother and son selling Asheville homes.
hero.sub: Ruth has sold houses in these mountains since 1996. Sam grew up riding along to showings and joined her in 2018. You get both of us, and we still argue about paint colors at Sunday dinner.

story.headline: Our story, from the beginning
story.sub: You'll be letting us into your home, so here's a bit of ours first.
items: A single mom with a seven-year-old, she sold her first house in Weaverville with Sam asleep in the back seat.
Fifteen and paid in pizza: setting out open house signs and fixing sticky doors before showings.
Sam gets his license after six years as a carpenter. Now there's someone on the team who can tell you what a repair really costs.
When Helene hit, we spent months helping clients through insurance claims and repairs. Some we'd sold homes to twenty years before.
Over 600 homes between us (sample). Most new clients come from someone we've already helped.

fix.headline: Fix it or leave it?
fix.sub: The question every seller asks us at the kitchen table. Make your guess, then see what we'd tell you, and roughly what it costs around here.

items.why: Buyers redo kitchens their own way. Paint or new hardware at most.

items.thing: A dripping faucet and a running toilet
items.why: Cheap to fix, and inspectors write up every one. Small items make buyers wonder about big ones.
A soft neutral photographs better and lets buyers picture their stuff. The best dollar you'll spend.

items.thing: An older roof that doesn't leak
items.why: Price for it instead. Buyers will ask for a credit either way, and a new roof rarely pays back.
It's the first photo and the first impression. Mulch, trim, and pots by the door.
Pull it up. Mountain buyers love original floors, even with a few scratches.

month.name: 1920s bungalow in West Asheville
month.body: Original heart pine floors, a deep front porch, and a fenced backyard with raised garden beds. Walk to Haywood Road.
notes: The porch faces west. You'll have the best sunsets on the street.
New electrical panel in 2023 and a dry crawlspace. I checked twice.

people.name: Ruth Hollis
people.bio: Ruth handles pricing, negotiating, and the hard conversations. She has seen every kind of market here, and she'll tell you which one you're in.
people.aside: Makes a mean pound cake for closings.

people.name: Sam Hollis
people.bio: Sam walks every house with you, reads the inspection report line by line, and knows which repairs are $200 and which are $20,000.
people.aside: Will crawl under your house so you don't have to.

items.text: Sam told us to skip the new countertops and paint instead. Saved us thousands and it sold in a week.

booking.headline: Come sit at our table
booking.body: Answer three quick questions and Ruth or Sam will call you today. If you're selling, we'll come walk your house with a notepad and tell you what to fix and what to leave.

lead.notesHint: Your address if you're selling, or what you need in a home
lead.consent: By sending this, you agree that Ruth or Sam Hollis may call or text you about your real estate question at the number you gave. Message and data rates may apply. Reply STOP to opt out. Consent isn't a condition of working with us.
lead.privacy: Your details go to Ruth and Sam only. Never sold or shared.
lead.thanks: Got it. One of us will call you today. Ruth and Sam

faq.q: Will we work with Ruth or Sam?
faq.a: Both. Ruth leads on pricing and negotiating, Sam on the house itself. You'll have both cell numbers.
It's negotiable and agreed in writing before any work starts. We'll explain what's included so you can compare us to anyone.

faq.q: Do you help with homes damaged in the storm?
faq.a: Yes. We've helped many families sell or buy after Helene, and we can point you to contractors and adjusters we trust.

faq.q: Do I need to fix everything before we list?
faq.a: No. Usually a few small things, and we'll tell you which ones are worth it. That's what the walk-through is for.
